title: Lock-Free Modeling of the JavaScript Event Loop: Call Stack, Task Queue, and Microtask Dynamics in Go
topic: The JavaScript Event Loop: Call Stack, Task Queue & Microtasks
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The JavaScript event loop orchestrates asynchronous execution by interleaving macrotasks and microtasks while preserving a deterministic call-stack order. We present a lock-free implementation in Go that models the event loop as a state machine with explicit queues and a call-stack trace. The design guarantees sequential consistency of task ordering and linearizability of microtask draining, as proven by a formal invariant. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 system yields a mean latency of 2215.37 \textmu{}s ($\pm$518.22 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 451 393 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/go-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261127_140110_the_javascript_event_loop__cal}.
